analyst_observations: With-skill achieves 100% assertion pass rate vs 84.1% baseline — the 16-point improvement comes mostly from eval-3 (code quality) where baseline missed escapeIlikePattern and procurements schema checks

Eval-2 (enrollment logic) was strong for both — the explicit question about two-stage approval and section_id made it easy to find even without skill guidance. Assertions may be too easy for targeted prompts
With-skill uses fewer tokens on average (102k vs 107k) because the 7-pass structure prevents unfocused exploration — particularly visible in eval-3 (81k vs 114k, 29% savings)
With-skill is slower on eval-1 security (652s vs 363s) because it ran all 7 passes vs security-only. For targeted requests, skill adds overhead. Consider adding scope detection to limit passes

Eval-1 baseline found issues the with-skill missed: sms_students publicly readable via anon GRANT (migration 015), sms_form137_requests USING(true), and rate limiting on student login. These are RLS-deep findings not covered by the skill's security checklist
Both correctly caught the Grade 10 graduation bug — the most impactful real finding. The skill surfaced it more prominently as a Critical finding with DepEd context
